m:marien: The square is always open. The Glockenspiel plays every day at 11am and noon, and from March to October also at 5pm (City Council website); the show lasts about 12–15 minutes (from guides) and the square fills up: arrive 10 minutes early. The Town Hall courtyard is free to visit.
m:frauen: Entry to the church is free, but it can't be visited during services (times on the cathedral website, not read). You can go up the south tower by lift: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday and holidays 11:30am–5pm, last ascent 4:30pm; tickets from €7.50 (from the official tourism website), online or at the cathedral shop.
m:viktu: The stalls are open Monday–Friday about 8am–8pm and Saturday 8am–3pm; the market is closed on Sundays (City Council website; each stall has its own hours). The Alter Peter tower (about 300 steps, no lift) is open from April to October 9am–7:30pm, from November to March 9am–6:30pm on weekdays and 9am–7:30pm at weekends; ticket €5, at the ticket desk only (City Council website, 2026 prices).
m:residenz: From 1 April to 19 October open every day 9am–6pm (last entry 5pm); from 20 October to 31 March 10am–5pm (last entry 4pm) (City Council website). 2026 prices from the Bavarian palaces administration: Residenz Museum €10, Treasury €10, combined ticket €15, full ticket with the Cuvilliés Theatre €20; under-18s go free. Large backpacks must be left in the cloakroom. The Hofgarten is free.
m:englg: The park is free and always open. Surfing on the Eisbach has been allowed again since 8 May 2026 (City Council website, updated August 2026), only for experienced surfers and never after 10pm: watch from the bridge. Swimming is forbidden. The Chinese Tower beer garden normally opens 10am–11pm, but from October it depends on the weather.
m:nymph: From April to 15 October 9am–6pm, from 16 October to March 10am–4pm; last entry about 20 minutes before (City Council website). Closed on Shrove Tuesday, 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January. 2026 prices (Bavarian palaces administration): palace €10, Marstallmuseum €8, full ticket €16 in winter and €20 in summer; the park pavilions are closed in winter. Under-18s go free. The park is free.
m:pinak: Closed on Mondays; Tuesday and Wednesday 10am–8pm, Thursday to Sunday 10am–6pm (City Council website). Ticket €7, reduced €5; €1 on Sundays; under-18s free. Closed on Shrove Tuesday, 1 May, and 24, 25 and 31 December. The lawn in front of the museum is a good place for a break.
m:asam: Free entry (donations welcome). From April to October 9am–7pm, from November to March 9am–6pm; on Fridays it only opens at 1pm (City Council website). It can't be visited during Mass. There are a few steps at the entrance.
m:deutsches: Open every day 9am–5pm, last entry 4:30pm (City Council website). Ticket €16, reduced €9, family €33. Closed on 1 November, 24, 25 and 31 December, 1 January, Good Friday and 1 May. It's being restored until 2028: some sections may be closed.
m:olympia: The park and BMW Welt are free. The BMW Museum is paid and normally closed on Mondays (from guides, 2026 prices and hours not read: check bmw-welt.com). The Olympic Tower (Olympiaturm) is closed for restoration until 2027 (City Council website).
vd:frischhut: A tiny café opposite the Viktualienmarkt where they fry Schmalznudel, a flattened ring of yeast dough, and jam-filled Krapfen in the window, to eat hot with a coffee.
vp:frischhut: A pastry and a coffee cost a few euros (menu not seen). Cash only. Closed on Sundays.
vd:fraeulein: A small café next to the Viktualienmarkt, famous for its cinnamon rolls in many flavours, homemade cakes and generous breakfast sandwiches.
vp:fraeulein: A roll and a cappuccino are around €7–9, a savoury breakfast around €12–15 (from reviews, menu not seen).
vd:weisses: The Schneider Weisse beer hall, a short walk from Marienplatz: wooden rooms, big shared tables and Bavarian cooking. From 9am you can have the traditional breakfast of Weißwurst, Brezn and wheat beer.
vp:weisses: Main courses cost about €16–25, half a litre of beer about €5.50 (from reviews, menu not seen).
vd:schaebitz: A Viktualienmarkt butcher's with a hot sandwich counter: Leberkässemmel, a slice of baked meatloaf in a roll with sweet mustard, cheese sausages and Weißwurst. Eaten standing up.
vp:schaebitz: Two hot sandwiches about €8–9 in total (from reviews, menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:friedl: A market butcher's serving roast pork with crispy crackling (Schweinebraten) in a roll, Leberkäse and Weißwurst: one of the Viktualienmarkt's best-loved snacks.
vp:friedl: A roast pork roll costs about €4–5 (from reviews, menu not seen). Closed on Mondays and Sundays.
vd:klosterwirt: A Bavarian tavern next to the cathedral with Augustiner beer, the locals' favourite: Wiener Schnitzel, crispy pork knuckle, Spätzle and strudel, in wooden rooms or at the outdoor tables.
vp:klosterwirt: A main course about €16–26 (menu not seen). Best to book in the evening.
vd:gloeckl: A historic inn behind the cathedral where little Nuremberg sausages are cooked on a wood-fired grill and arrive on pewter plates with sauerkraut and potato salad; the Augustiner beer comes from wooden barrels.
vp:gloeckl: A plate of sausages with a side about €14–20 (menu not seen).
vd:franziskaner: A large traditional tavern between Marienplatz and the Residenz, with wooden rooms and hearty Bavarian cooking: Weißwurst in the morning, Sauerbraten, schnitzel and Kaiserschmarrn.
vp:franziskaner: A main course about €16–25 (menu not seen).
vd:ayinger: The Aying brewery's tavern, opposite the Hofbräuhaus but quieter: roast pork, meat platters to share and the brewery's beers.
vp:ayinger: A main course about €16–24 (menu not seen).
vd:hb: The world's most famous beer hall, from 1589: huge rooms with painted vaults, the brass band, one-litre steins and a tree-lined courtyard. It's very touristy but worth doing once, even just for a beer and a Brezn.
vp:hb: A litre of beer and a hot dish come to around €25–30 (menu not seen). Hours from online listings; the City Council website gives a 10:30am opening at weekends.
vd:puck: A neighbourhood café near the University and the Pinakotheken, popular with students: big breakfasts all day with bread from a good bakery, and simple dishes at lunch and dinner.
vp:puck: A full breakfast about €12–16, a lunch dish about €12–16 (menu not seen).
vd:maxemanuel: An old Maxvorstadt beer hall, away from the tourist circuit, with a tree-lined courtyard: schnitzel fried in butter, roast pork and Paulaner beer, among students and locals.
vp:maxemanuel: A main course about €14–22 (menu not seen). Best to book in the evening.
vd:loewen: The big Löwenbräu beer hall, with the tower and the lion on the façade: less touristy than those in the centre, huge portions of pork knuckle, roast and Brezn, halfway between the centre and Nymphenburg.
vp:loewen: A main course about €16–25 (menu not seen).
vd:chinaturm: The English Garden's most famous beer garden, with thousands of seats under the chestnut trees around the wooden pagoda. Get food from the self-service counters: half a chicken, sausages, Brezn and Obatzda, the beer cheese spread.
vp:chinaturm: A litre of beer and a dish come to around €20–25 (menu not seen). In autumn and winter it only opens in good weather: check first.
vd:seehaus: A restaurant and beer garden on the shore of the Kleinhesseloher lake, in the northern part of the English Garden: the restaurant is a bit pricey, the self-service counter by the lake is cheaper and has the best view.
vp:seehaus: At the self-service a dish is about €12–18, at the restaurant mains often go over €25 (from reviews, menu not seen).
vd:au: A 1901 tavern five minutes from the Deutsches Museum, famous for its dumplings (Knödel) in many versions, roast pork and duck. A neighbourhood atmosphere, very popular with locals.
vp:au: A main course about €15–24 (menu not seen). On weekdays it only opens at 5pm; best to book in the evening.
vd:ruffini: A café with a bakery and pâtisserie in Neuhausen, on the way to Nymphenburg, with a rooftop terrace: homemade cakes, breakfasts and simple dishes, among locals.
vp:ruffini: A coffee with a slice of cake about €7–10, a dish about €12–18 (menu not seen). Closed on Mondays.
vd:palmenhaus: The café in the palm house of Nymphenburg park, bright and quiet: cakes, strudel and hot dishes, with a quicker self-service section.
vp:palmenhaus: A coffee with strudel about €8–11 (menu not seen). Open Thursday to Sunday only (hours from online listings, to be confirmed).
cd:olympiaturm: The tower in the Olympic Park, with views as far as the Alps.
cd:bmwmuseum: The brand's history, from motorbikes to racing cars.
cd:rathausturm: The lift up to the terrace above Marienplatz.
cd:pinakothekmoderne: Modern art, architecture and design in a single building.
cd:lenbachhaus: The Blue Rider: Kandinsky and Franz Marc in a Tuscan-style villa.
cd:hellabrunn: A zoo laid out by geographical areas along the Isar.
cd:stadtmuseum: The history of Munich, with puppets and the beer hall.
cd:allianz: Bayern's stadium: dressing rooms, stands and museum.
cx:allianz: It's 11 km from the centre, reachable by underground.
cd:aegyptisches: An Egyptian collection in modern rooms dug underground.
